tagline: Brunswick County communities and a hydroelectric lake frame this byway.
intro: Brunswick County identifies Highways 903 and 626 as the Lake Gaston Byway, one of its two Virginia Byways. The setting includes small communities such as Ebony, Gasburg and Valentines, with Lake Gaston extending into Brunswick and Mecklenburg counties.

The lake took shape in 1963 when Virginia Electric Power Company built Gaston Dam on the Roanoke River to generate electricity. On Route 626, the private Lake Gaston Resort occupies shoreline in the Pea Hill Creek area.
The communities run west to east from Ebony to Gasburg and then Valentines. Valentines has a combined store and post office, and the historic Mason–Tillett House.

moments.title: Ebony
moments.text: Ebony is an unincorporated Brunswick County community. The 2020 census counted 150 residents.

moments.title: Gasburg and Pea Hill Creek
moments.text: Gasburg is an unincorporated community in Brunswick County. Lake Gaston’s marina listing places Lake Gaston Resort at Gasburg; the resort itself is on Route 626 in the Pea Hill Creek area. It is a private camping and recreational-vehicle resort.

moments.title: Valentines
moments.text: Valentines has a combined store and post office. The community’s Mason–Tillett House is a historic plantation house, also known as Rock Hill. Built about 1780, it received a one-and-a-half-story addition about 1832.
